draft.title: Conserving the sites
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum were buried in AD 79 and have been open to the weather since excavation. Rain, frost, sun and plant growth slowly damage walls, paint and floors.
Some past restorations did harm. Early repairs used materials such as concrete, which can trap water and damage the ancient fabric.
Large areas of Pompeii remain unrepaired, so walls can fall. In 2010 the House of the Gladiators collapsed after heavy rain, which showed how weak the site's upkeep was.
Conservation means protecting what survives. Today it includes regular maintenance and careful repair, because new excavation exposes more material that then needs care.
draft.remember: The sites are damaged by weather, by past repairs and by neglect, so protecting them takes steady care.

a.q: Why was the 2010 collapse of the House of the Gladiators important for conservation?
opts: It showed that the site was at risk without steady upkeep
It proved that the volcano had become active again
It showed that tourists had pulled the building down
It showed that ancient building methods were poor
a.why: The collapse followed heavy rain on a weakened structure, so it showed the need for regular maintenance. It was not caused by the volcano, which had been quiet for decades.
a.clue: Think about what had been happening to the building before the rain.

b.q: A site manager finds that an early repair to a Pompeii wall used cement that traps water, and the original plaster behind it is flaking. What does this best show?
opts: Past restoration can itself threaten the site
Weather is not a threat to restored walls
Only new excavations cause damage to walls
Repairs of any kind should be avoided
b.why: The cement was meant to protect the wall but is now harming the plaster. That makes past poor restoration a threat. It does not show that all repair is bad, only that materials and methods must be chosen with care.
b.clue: The repair was meant to help the wall.

a.best: It showed that the site was at risk without steady upkeep

b.best: Past restoration can itself threaten the site

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedged qualifier ('can'), while every distractor is an absolute ('Only', 'any kind', 'is not'). A test-wise student could pick it without knowing the idea.

The last bullet says conservation includes regular maintenance 'because new excavation exposes more material'. This implies upkeep is needed mainly because of new digging, when the card's main reasons are weather, past repairs and neglect. The causal link is confusing.
Why (b) says materials and methods 'must be chosen with care', which is stronger than the card, where concrete only 'can' trap water. This is minor.

proposal.title: Conserving the sites
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum were buried in AD 79 and have been open to the weather since excavation. Rain, sun and plant growth slowly damage walls, paint and floors. Visitors' feet add wear too.
Some past restorations did harm. Early repairs used materials such as concrete, which can trap water and damage the ancient fabric.
Large areas of Pompeii were left without proper upkeep, so walls can fall. In 2010 the House of the Gladiators collapsed after heavy rain, which showed how weak the site's upkeep was.
Conservation means protecting what survives. It needs regular maintenance, such as drainage, roofing and clearing plants, and repairs with materials that suit the ancient fabric.
proposal.remember: Weather, wear, poor past repairs and neglect all threaten the sites, so protecting them takes steady care.

a.q: Why was the 2010 collapse of the House of the Gladiators important for conservation?
opts: It showed that the site was at risk without steady upkeep
It showed that the volcano had become active again
It showed that tourists had pulled the building down
It showed that Roman builders had used poor methods
a.why: The collapse followed heavy rain on a poorly maintained structure, so it showed the need for regular upkeep. It was not caused by the volcano or by tourists pulling it down, and it says more about modern care than Roman building.
a.clue: Think about how the building had been looked after before the rain.

b.q: A site manager finds that an early repair to a Pompeii wall used cement that traps water, and the original plaster behind it is flaking. What does this best show?
opts: Poor past restoration is itself a threat to the site
Restored walls are protected from weather damage
Visitor foot traffic is the main cause of wall damage
Ancient plaster was too weak to survive in the open
b.why: The cement was meant to protect the wall but is now trapping water and harming the plaster. That makes poor past restoration a threat. It does not show that restored walls are safe from weather: the trapped water is what is doing the damage.
b.clue: The repair was meant to help the wall.
